content: Most modern engines want synthetic oil changed every 7,500-10,000 miles; conventional oil every 3,000-5,000 miles. Check the owner's manual — it overrides these rules of thumb.
Rotate tires every 5,000-7,500 miles to even out wear, roughly every other oil change.
Coolant typically needs replacing every 30,000-60,000 miles depending on type (green vs. long-life orange/pink). Old coolant loses corrosion protection even if it hasn't frozen or boiled.
Brake pads generally last 25,000-70,000 miles depending on driving style. A high-pitched squeal on braking usually means the wear indicator is contacting the rotor — time to inspect.

If the engine has a timing belt (not a chain), it's usually replaced every 60,000-100,000 miles. A snapped timing belt can cause serious engine damage on interference engines — this one isn't optional.
Car batteries typically last 3-5 years. Cold weather is hardest on a weak battery — that's when it usually finally fails.
Cabin air filters should be replaced roughly every 15,000-25,000 miles or annually. A musty AC smell is a common sign it's overdue.
A steady check engine light means investigate soon; a flashing check engine light means stop driving soon — it usually indicates an active engine misfire that can damage the catalytic converter.
P0128 means the engine is taking too long to reach normal operating temperature, almost always a stuck-open thermostat. Not an emergency, but hurts fuel economy and heater performance.
P0300 indicates a random or multiple cylinder misfire. Common causes: worn spark plugs, bad ignition coils, or a vacuum leak. Driving on a misfire risks catalytic converter damage.
P0442 is a small evaporative emissions leak — very often just a loose or worn gas cap. Worth checking before assuming anything more serious.
